# Vela UI

Vela UI is a modern React component library built on top of React Aria Components, designed to provide accessible, customizable, and high-quality UI components for React applications. It leverages Tailwind CSS for styling and tailwind-variants for component variant management.

## Why React Aria?

React Aria is style-free out of the box, allowing you to build custom designs to fit your application or design system using any styling and animation solution. Each component is broken down into individual parts with built-in states, render props, and slots that make styling a breeze.

## Why Tailwind CSS?

All components are built with Tailwind CSS v4, which provides a robust set of utility classes for styling. This allows you to quickly and easily customize the appearance of your components without having to write custom CSS.

- [Vela UI](https://github.com/vela-ui/vela-ui)
- [React Aria Components](https://react-spectrum.adobe.com/react-aria/components.html)
- [Tailwind CSS](https://tailwindcss.com/)
- [tailwind-variants](https://www.tailwind-variants.org/docs/getting-started)

## Installation

Add dependencies to your project manually.

### Add Tailwind CSS

Components are styled using Tailwind CSS. You need to install Tailwind CSS in your project.

[Follow the Tailwind CSS installation instructions to get started.](https://tailwindcss.com/docs/installation)

### Add dependencies

```sh
npm install tw-animate-css @vela-ui/react
```

## Theme Configuration

Add the following to your styles/globals.css file

```css
@import "tailwindcss";
@import "tw-animate-css";
@custom-variant dark (&:is(.dark *));
@source "../node_modules/@vela-ui/react";

:root {
  --background: oklch(1 0 0);
  --foreground: oklch(0.145 0 0);
  --card: oklch(1 0 0);
  --card-foreground: oklch(0.145 0 0);
  --popover: oklch(1 0 0);
  --popover-foreground: oklch(0.145 0 0);
  --primary: oklch(0.205 0 0);
  --primary-foreground: oklch(0.985 0 0);
  --secondary: oklch(0.97 0 0);
  --secondary-foreground: oklch(0.205 0 0);
  --muted: oklch(0.97 0 0);
  --muted-foreground: oklch(0.556 0 0);
  --accent: oklch(0.97 0 0);
  --accent-foreground: oklch(0.205 0 0);
  --destructive: oklch(0.577 0.245 27.325);
  --border: oklch(0.922 0 0);
  --input: oklch(0.922 0 0);
  --ring: oklch(0.708 0 0);
  --chart-1: oklch(0.646 0.222 41.116);
  --chart-2: oklch(0.6 0.118 184.704);
  --chart-3: oklch(0.398 0.07 227.392);
  --chart-4: oklch(0.828 0.189 84.429);
  --chart-5: oklch(0.769 0.188 70.08);
  --radius: 0.625rem;
  --sidebar: oklch(0.985 0 0);
  --sidebar-foreground: oklch(0.145 0 0);
  --sidebar-primary: oklch(0.205 0 0);
  --sidebar-primary-foreground: oklch(0.985 0 0);
```

## Styling

React Aria Components do not include any styles by default, allowing you to build custom designs to fit your application or design system using any styling solution.

[Styling docs](https://react-spectrum.adobe.com/react-aria/styling.html)

# Components

---

# Alert

## Anatomy

An alert displays a message that draws the user's attention without interrupting their current activity.

## Example

Here's a basic example of how to use the Alert component:

```tsx
import { Alert, AlertTitle } from "@vela-ui/react"
import { CircleCheckIcon } from "lucide-react"

export function Basic() {
  return (
    <Alert>
      <CircleCheckIcon />
      <AlertTitle>Success! Your changes have been saved</AlertTitle>
    </Alert>
  )
}
```

### With Description

An Alert can include both a title and description:

```tsx
import { Alert, AlertContent, AlertDescription, AlertTitle } from "@vela-ui/react"
import { CircleAlertIcon } from "lucide-react"

export function WithDescription() {
  return (
    <Alert>
      <CircleAlertIcon />
      <AlertContent>
        <AlertTitle>Browser Update available</AlertTitle>
        <AlertDescription>For the best experience, please update your browser.</AlertDescription>
      </AlertContent>
    </Alert>
  )
}
```

## API Reference

### Alert

The `Alert` component is a wrapper for the alert component.

### AlertContent

The `AlertContent` component is a container for the alert content.

### AlertTitle

The `AlertTitle` component is the title of the alert message.

### AlertDescription

The `AlertDescription` component is the description of the alert message.

## Accessibility

# Avatar

## Anatomy

An image element with a fallback for representing the user.

## Example

Here's a basic example of how to use the Avatar component:

```tsx
import { Avatar, AvatarFallback, AvatarImage } from "@vela-ui/react"

export function Basic() {
  return (
    <Avatar>
      <AvatarImage src="https://github.com/shadcn.png" alt="@shadcn" />
      <AvatarFallback>CN</AvatarFallback>
    </Avatar>
  )
}
```

### Avatar Group

You can create avatar groups with overlapping styles:

```tsx
import { Avatar, AvatarFallback, AvatarImage } from "@vela-ui/react"

export function Group() {
  return (
    <div className="flex -space-x-2">
      <Avatar className="ring-background ring-2">
        <AvatarImage src="https://github.com/shadcn.png" alt="@shadcn" />
        <AvatarFallback>CN</AvatarFallback>
      </Avatar>
      <Avatar className="ring-background ring-2">
        <AvatarImage src="https://github.com/leerob.png" alt="@leerob" />
        <AvatarFallback>LR</AvatarFallback>
      </Avatar>
      <Avatar className="ring-background ring-2">
        <AvatarImage src="https://github.com/evilrabbit.png" alt="@evilrabbit" />
        <AvatarFallback>ER</AvatarFallback>
      </Avatar>
    </div>
  )
}
```

## API Reference

### Avatar

#### Props

**`size`**
Type: "sm" | "md" | "lg"
Default: "md"
Description: The size of the avatar.

**`shape`**
Type: "circle" | "square"
Default: "circle"
Description: The shape of the avatar.

### AvatarFallback

#### Props

**`delayMs`**
Type: number
Default: `undefined`
Description: Delay in milliseconds before showing the fallback.

### AvatarImage

#### Props

**`src`**
Type: string
Description: The source URL of the image.

**`alt`**
Type: string
Description: Alternative text for the image.

**`onLoadingStatusChange`**
Type: (status: ImageLoadingStatus) => void
Description: Callback fired when the image loading status changes.

# Badge

## Anatomy

A badge is a small component that can be used to display a count or a status.

## Example

Here's a basic example of how to use the Badge component:

```tsx
import { Badge } from "@vela-ui/react"

export function Basic() {
  return <Badge>Default</Badge>
}
```

### With Icon

You can include icons in badges:

```tsx
import { Badge } from "@vela-ui/react"
import { HeartIcon } from "lucide-react"

export function WithIcon() {
  return (
    <div className="flex items-center gap-2">
      <Badge>
        <HeartIcon />
        Badge
      </Badge>
      <Badge variant="secondary">
        <HeartIcon />
        Badge
      </Badge>
      <Badge variant="destructive">
        <HeartIcon />
        Badge
      </Badge>
      <Badge variant="outline">
        <HeartIcon />
        Badge
      </Badge>
    </div>
  )
}
```

### With Button

Badges can be used inside buttons to show counts or status:

```tsx
import { Badge, Button } from "@vela-ui/react"

export function WithButton() {
  return (
    <div className="flex items-center gap-2">
      <Button variant="outline">
        Inbox
        <Badge>+99</Badge>
      </Button>
      <Button variant="outline">
        Messages
        <Badge variant="destructive">3</Badge>
      </Button>
      <Button variant="outline">
        Notifications
        <Badge variant="secondary">12</Badge>
      </Button>
    </div>
  )
}
```

## API Reference

### Badge

#### Props

**`variant`**
Type: "neutral" | "primary" | "secondary" | "accent" | "destructive" | "outline"
Default: "primary"
Description: The visual style variant of the badge.

# Button

[Button docs](https://react-spectrum.adobe.com/react-aria/Button.html)

## Anatomy

A button allows a user to perform an action, with mouse, touch, and keyboard interactions.

## Example

Here's a basic example of how to use the Button component:

```tsx
import { Button } from "@vela-ui/react"

export function Basic() {
  return <Button onPress={() => alert("Hello world!")}>Press me</Button>
}
```

## API Reference

### Button

#### Props

**`variant`**
Type: "neutral" | "primary" | "secondary" | "destructive" | "outline" | "ghost" | "link"
Default: "primary"
Description: The variant of the button.

**`size`**
Type: "xs" | "sm" | "md" | "lg" | "xl"
Default: "md"
Description: The size of the button.

**`shape`**
Type: "rectangle" | "square" | "circle"
Default: "rectangle"
Description: The shape of the button.

**`loader`**
Type: React.ReactNode
Default: <Loader />
Description: The loader to display when the button is in a pending state.

**`isPending`**
Type: boolean
Description: Whether the button is in a pending state.

**`isDisabled`**
Type: boolean
Description: Whether the button is disabled.

**`autoFocus`**
Type: boolean
Description: Whether the element should receive focus on render.

**`type`**
Type: "button" | "submit" | "reset"
Default: "button"
Description: The behavior of the button when used in an HTML form.

**`form`**
Type: string
Description: The `<form>` element to associate the button with. The value of this attribute must be the id of a `<form>` in the same document.

#### Events

**`onPress`**
Type: (e: PressEvent) => void
Description: Handler that is called when the press is released over the target.

**`onPressStart`**
Type: (e: PressEvent) => void
Description: Handler that is called when a press interaction starts.

**`onPressEnd`**
Type: (e: PressEvent) => void
Description: Handler that is called when a press interaction ends, either over the target or when the pointer leaves the target.

**`onPressChange`**
Type: (isPressed: boolean) => void
Description: Handler that is called when the press state changes.

**`onPressUp`**
Type: (e: PressEvent) => void
Description: Handler that is called when a press is released over the target, regardless of whether it started on the target or not.

#### Accessibility

**`id`**
Type: string
Description: The element's unique identifier.

**`aria-disabled`**
Type: boolean
Description: Indicates whether the element is disabled to users of assistive technology.

**`aria-expanded`**
Type: boolean
Description: Indicates whether the element, or another grouping element it controls, is currently expanded or collapsed.

**`aria-label`**
Type: string
Description: Defines a string value that labels the current element.

**`aria-labelledby`**
Type: string
Description: Identifies the element (or elements) that labels the current element.

**`aria-describedby`**
Type: string
Description: Identifies the element (or elements) that describes the object.

**`aria-details`**
Type: boolean
Description: Identifies the element (or elements) that provide a detailed, extended description for the object.

# Card

## Anatomy

Displays a card with header, content, and footer.

## Example

Here's a basic example of how to use the Card component:

```tsx
import { Card, CardContent, CardDescription, CardHeader, CardTitle } from "@vela-ui/react"

export function Basic() {
  return (
    <Card className="w-full max-w-sm">
      <CardHeader>
        <CardTitle>Card Title</CardTitle>
        <CardDescription>Card description goes here.</CardDescription>
      </CardHeader>
      <CardContent>
        <p>Card content goes here.</p>
      </CardContent>
    </Card>
  )
}
```

## API Reference

### Card

The main container for the card component.

### CardHeader

Container for the card header including title, description, and action.

### CardTitle

The title of the card.

### CardDescription

The description of the card.

### CardAction

Container for action buttons in the card header.

### CardContent

The main content area of the card.

### CardFooter

Container for footer content and actions.

# Link

[Link docs](https://react-spectrum.adobe.com/react-aria/Link.html)

## Anatomy

A link allows a user to navigate to another page or resource within a web page or application.

## Example

Here's a basic example of how to use the Link component:

```tsx
import { Link } from "@vela-ui/react"

export function Basic() {
  return (
    <Link href="https://tailwindcss.com" target="_blank">
      Visit Tailwind CSS
    </Link>
  )
}
```

## API Reference

### Link

#### Props

**`variant`**
Type: "hover" | "underline" | "none"
Default: "hover"
Description: The visual style variant of the link.

**`isDisabled`**
Type: boolean
Default: false
Description: Whether the link is disabled.

**`autoFocus`**
Type: boolean
Description: Whether the element should receive focus on render.

**`href`**
Type: string
Description: The URL that the link points to.

**`hrefLang`**
Type: string
Description: Hints at the human language of the linked URL

**`target`**
Type: "\_blank" | "\_self" | "\_parent" | "\_top"
Description: Where to display the linked URL.

**`rel`**
Type: string
Description: The relationship between the linked resource and the current page.

**`download`**
Type: boolean | string
Description: Whether the link should be downloaded when clicked.

**`routerOptions`**
Type: RouterOptions
Description: Options for the configured client side router.

#### Events

**`onPress`**
Type: (e: PressEvent) => void
Description: Handler that is called when the press is released over the target.

**`onPressStart`**
Type: (e: PressEvent) => void
Description: Handler that is called when a press interaction starts.

**`onPressEnd`**
Type: (e: PressEvent) => void
Description: Handler that is called when a press interaction ends, either over the target or when the pointer leaves the target.

**`onPressChange`**
Type: (isPressed: boolean) => void
Description: Handler that is called when the press state changes.

**`onPressUp`**
Type: (e: PressEvent) => void
Description: Handler that is called when a press is released over the target, regardless of whether it started on the target or not.

#### Accessibility

**`aria-label`**
Type: string
Description: Defines a string value that labels the current element.

**`aria-labelledby`**
Type: string
Description: Identifies the element (or elements) that labels the current element.

**`aria-describedby`**
Type: string
Description: Identifies the element (or elements) that describes the object.

**`aria-details`**
Type: boolean
Description: Identifies the element (or elements) that provide a detailed, extended description for the object.

# LinkButton

## Anatomy

A LinkButton combines the functionality of a Link with the visual appearance of a Button. It's useful when you want a button-like appearance that navigates to another page or resource.

## Example

Here's a basic example of how to use the LinkButton component:

```tsx
import { LinkButton } from "@vela-ui/react"

export function Basic() {
  return <LinkButton href="/dashboard">Go to Dashboard</LinkButton>
}
```

## API Reference

### LinkButton

#### Props

**`variant`**
Type: "neutral" | "primary" | "secondary" | "accent" | "destructive" | "outline" | "ghost" | "link"
Default: "primary"
Description: The visual style variant of the link button.

**`size`**
Type: "xs" | "sm" | "md" | "lg" | "xl"
Default: "md"
Description: The size of the link button.

**`shape`**
Type: "rectangle" | "square" | "circle"
Default: "rectangle"
Description: The shape of the link button.

**`isDisabled`**
Type: boolean
Default: false
Description: Whether the link button is disabled.

**`href`**
Type: string
Description: The URL that the link button points to.

**`target`**
Type: "\_blank" | "\_self" | "\_parent" | "\_top"
Description: Where to display the linked URL.

**`rel`**
Type: string
Description: The relationship between the current document and the linked document.

# CheckboxGroup

[CheckboxGroup docs](https://react-spectrum.adobe.com/react-aria/CheckboxGroup.html)

## Anatomy

A checkbox group allows a user to select multiple items from a list of options.

## Example

Here's how to use CheckboxGroup with multiple checkboxes:

```tsx
import { Checkbox, CheckboxGroup } from "@vela-ui/react"

export function BasicGroup() {
  return (
    <CheckboxGroup label="Cities" description="Select your favorite cities">
      <Checkbox value="sf">San Francisco</Checkbox>
      <Checkbox value="ny">New York</Checkbox>
      <Checkbox value="sydney">Sydney</Checkbox>
      <Checkbox value="london">London</Checkbox>
      <Checkbox value="tokyo">Tokyo</Checkbox>
    </CheckboxGroup>
  )
}
```

### CheckboxGroup with Validation

A CheckboxGroup can include validation:

```tsx
import { Button, Checkbox, CheckboxGroup, Form } from "@vela-ui/react"

export function WithValidation() {
  return (
    <Form className="flex flex-col items-start gap-4">
      <CheckboxGroup
        label="Required Selection"
        description="Please select at least one option"
        isRequired
        errorMessage="Please select at least one option"
      >
        <Checkbox value="option1">Option 1</Checkbox>
        <Checkbox value="option2">Option 2</Checkbox>
        <Checkbox value="option3">Option 3</Checkbox>
      </CheckboxGroup>
      <Button type="submit">Submit</Button>
    </Form>
  )
}
```

## API Reference

### CheckboxGroup

#### Props

**`label`**
Type: string
Description: The label for the checkbox group.

**`description`**
Type: string
Description: A description for the checkbox group.

**`errorMessage`**
Type: string | ((validation: ValidationResult) => string)
Description: Error message to display when validation fails.

**`value`**
Type: string[]
Description: The current value (controlled).

**`defaultValue`**
Type: string[]
Description: The default value (uncontrolled).

**`name`**
Type: string
Description: The name of the input element, used when submitting an HTML form.

**`isDisabled`**
Type: boolean
Description: Whether the input is disabled.

**`isReadOnly`**
Type: boolean
Description: Whether the input can be selected but not changed by the user.

**`isRequired`**
Type: boolean
Description: Whether user input is required on the input before form submission.

**`isInvalid`**
Type: boolean
Description: Whether the input value is invalid.

**`validate`**
Type: (value: string[]) => ValidationError
Description: A function that returns an error message if a given value is invalid

**`form`**
Type: string
Description: The `<form>` element to associate the input with. The value of this attribute must be the id of a `<form>` in the same document

**`validationBehavior`**
Type: "native" | "aria"
Default: "native"
Description: Whether to use native HTML form validation to prevent form submission when the value is missing or invalid, or mark the field as required or invalid via ARIA.

#### Events

**`onChange`**
Type: (value: T) => void
Description: Handler that is called when the value changes.

**`onFocus`**
Type: (e: FocusEvent) => void
Description: Handler that is called when the element receives focus.

**`onFocusChange`**
Type: (isFocused: boolean) => void
Description: Handler that is called when the element's focus status changes.

**`onBlur`**
Type: (e: FocusEvent) => void
Description: Handler that is called when the element loses focus.

#### Accessibility

**`id`**
Type: string
Description: The element's unique identifier'

**`aria-label`**
Type: string
Description: Defines a string value that labels the current element.

**`aria-labelledby`**
Type: string
Description: Identifies the element (or elements) that labels the current element.

**`aria-describedby`**
Type: string
Description: Identifies the element (or elements) that describes the object.

**`aria-details`**
Type: boolean
Description: Identifies the element (or elements) that provide a detailed, extended description for the object.

**`aria-errormessage`**
Type: string
Description: Identifies the element that provides an error message for the object.

# Checkbox

[Checkbox docs](https://react-spectrum.adobe.com/react-aria/Checkbox.html)

## Anatomy

A checkbox allows a user to select multiple items from a list of individual items, or to mark one individual item as selected.

## Example

Here's a basic example of how to use the Checkbox component:

```tsx
import { Checkbox } from "@vela-ui/react"

export function Basic() {
  return <Checkbox>Checkbox</Checkbox>
}
```

### Checkbox States

The Checkbox component supports different states:

```tsx
import { Checkbox } from "@vela-ui/react"

export function States() {
  return (
    <div className="flex flex-col gap-2">
      <Checkbox>Unchecked</Checkbox>
      <Checkbox defaultSelected>Checked</Checkbox>
      <Checkbox isIndeterminate>Indeterminate</Checkbox>
      <Checkbox isDisabled>Disabled</Checkbox>
    </div>
  )
}
```

## API Reference

### Checkbox

#### Props

**`size`**
Type: "sm" | "md" | "lg"
Default: "md"
Description: The size of the checkbox.

**`indicatorClassName`**
Type: string
Description: Custom CSS classes for the checkbox indicator.

**`inputRef`**
Type: React.RefObject`<HTMLInputElement>`
Description: A ref for the HTML input element.

**`value`**
Type: string
Description: The value of the input element, used when submitting an HTML form.

**`defaultSelected`**
Type: boolean
Description: Whether the element should be selected (uncontrolled).

**`isIndeterminate`**
Type: boolean
Description: Indeterminism is presentational only. The indeterminate visual representation remains regardless of user interaction.

**`isSelected`**
Type: boolean
Description: Whether the element should be selected (controlled).

**`isDisabled`**
Type: boolean
Description: Whether the input is disabled.

**`isReadOnly`**
Type: boolean
Description: Whether the input can be selected but not changed by the user.

**`isRequired`**
Type: boolean
Description: Whether user input is required on the input before form submission.

**`isInvalid`**
Type: boolean
Description: Whether the input value is invalid.

**`validate`**
Type: (value: boolean) => ValidationError
Description: A function that returns an error message if a given value is invalid.

**`autoFocus`**
Type: boolean
Description: Whether the element should receive focus on render.

**`name`**
Type: string
Description: The name of the input element, used when submitting an HTML form.

**`form`**
Type: string
Description: The `<form>` element to associate the input with. The value of this attribute must be the id of a `<form>` in the same document.

**`validationBehavior`**
Type: "native" | "aria"
Default: "native"
Description: Whether to use native HTML form validation to prevent form submission when the value is missing or invalid, or mark the field as required or invalid via ARIA.

#### Events

**`onChange`**
Type: (isSelected: boolean) => void
Description: Handler that is called when the element's selection state changes.

**`onFocus`**
Type: (e: FocusEvent) => void
Description: Handler that is called when the element receives focus.

**`onFocusChange`**
Type: (isFocused: boolean) => void
Description: Handler that is called when the element's focus status changes.

**`onBlur`**
Type: (e: FocusEvent) => void
Description: Handler that is called when the element loses focus.

#### Accessibility

**`id`**
Type: string
Description: The element's unique identifier.

**`aria-controls`**
Type: string
Description: Identifies the element (or elements) whose contents or presence are controlled by the current element.

**`aria-label`**
Type: string
Description: Defines a string value that labels the current element.

**`aria-labelledby`**
Type: string
Description: Identifies the element (or elements) that labels the current element.

**`aria-describedby`**
Type: string
Description: Identifies the element (or elements) that describes the object.

**`aria-details`**
Type: boolean
Description: Identifies the element (or elements) that provide a detailed, extended description for the object.

**`aria-errormessage`**
Type: string
Description: Identifies the element that provides an error message for the object.

# Combobox

[Combobox docs](https://react-spectrum.adobe.com/react-aria/Combobox.html)

## Anatomy

A combo box combines a text input with a listbox, allowing users to filter a list of options to items matching a query.

## Example

Here's a basic example of how to use the Combobox component:

```tsx
import {
  Combobox,
  ComboboxInput,
  ComboboxItem,
  ComboboxList,
  ComboboxPopover,
} from "@vela-ui/react"

export function Basic() {
  const items = ["Apple", "Banana", "Orange", "Grapes"]

  return (
    <Combobox className="w-64" placeholder="Select a fruit" label="Favorite Fruit">
      <ComboboxInput />
      <ComboboxPopover>
        <ComboboxList>
          {items.map((item) => (
            <ComboboxItem key={item}>{item}</ComboboxItem>
          ))}
        </ComboboxList>
      </ComboboxPopover>
    </Combobox>
  )
}
```

### With Sections

A Combobox can include sections to group related items:

```tsx
import {
  Combobox,
  ComboboxInput,
  ComboboxItem,
  ComboboxList,
  ComboboxPopover,
  ComboboxSection,
} from "@vela-ui/react"

export function WithSections() {
  const options = [
    {
      name: "Fruit",
      children: [{ name: "Apple" }, { name: "Banana" }, { name: "Orange" }],
    },
    {
      name: "Vegetable",
      children: [{ name: "Cabbage" }, { name: "Broccoli" }, { name: "Carrots" }],
    },
  ]

  return (
    <Combobox className="w-64" placeholder="Select an item" label="Food Category">
      <ComboboxInput />
      <ComboboxPopover>
        <ComboboxList>
          {options.map((section) => (
            <ComboboxSection key={section.name} title={section.name}>
              {section.children.map((item) => (
                <ComboboxItem key={item.name}>{item.name}</ComboboxItem>
              ))}
            </ComboboxSection>
          ))}
        </ComboboxList>
      </ComboboxPopover>
    </Combobox>
  )
}
```

## API Reference

### Combobox

#### Props

**`label`**
Type: string
Description: The label for the combobox.

**`description`**
Type: string
Description: A description for the combobox.

**`errorMessage`**
Type: string | ((validation: ValidationResult) => string)
Description: Error message to display when validation fails.

**`defaultFilter`**
Type: (textValue: string, inputValue: string) => boolean
Description: The filter function used to determine if a option should be included in the combo box list.

**`formValue`**
Type: 'text' | 'key'
Default: 'key'
Description: Whether the text or key of the selected item is submitted as part of an HTML form. When allowsCustomValue is true, this option does not apply and the text is always submitted.

**`allowsEmptyCollection`**
Type: boolean
Description: Whether the combo box allows the menu to be open when the collection is empty.

**`shouldFocusWrap`**
Type: boolean
Description: Whether keyboard navigation is circular.

**`defaultItems`**
Type: Iterable<T>
Description: The list of ComboBox items (uncontrolled).

**`items`**
Type: Iterable<T>
Description: The list of ComboBox items (controlled).

**`inputValue`**
Type: string
Description: The value of the ComboBox input (controlled).

**`defaultInputValue`**
Type: string
Description: The default value of the ComboBox input (uncontrolled).

**`allowsCustomValue`**
Type: boolean
Description: Whether the ComboBox allows a non-item matching input value to be set.

**`menuTrigger`**
Type: 'focus' | 'input' | 'manual'
Default: 'input'
Description: The interaction required to display the ComboBox menu.

**`disabledKeys`**
Type: Iterable<Key>
Description: The item keys that are disabled. These items cannot be selected, focused, or otherwise interacted with.

**`selectedKey`**
Type: Key
Description: The initial selected key in the collection (uncontrolled).

**`defaultSelectedKey`**
Type: Key
Description: The initial selected key in the collection (uncontrolled).

**`isDisabled`**
Type: boolean
Description: Whether the input is disabled.

**`isReadOnly`**
Type: boolean
Description: Whether the input can be selected but not changed by the user.

**`isRequired`**
Type: boolean
Description: Whether user input is required on the input before form submission.

**`isInvalid`**
Type: boolean
Description: Whether the input value is invalid.

**`validate`**
Type: (value: ComboBoxValidationValue) => ValidationError
Description: A function that returns an error message if a given value is invalid.

**`autoFocus`**
Type: boolean
Description: Whether the element should receive focus on render.

**`name`**
Type: string
Description: The name of the input element, used when submitting an HTML form.

**`form`**
Type: string
Description: The `<form>` element to associate the input with. The value of this attribute must be the id of a `<form>` in the same document.

**`validationBehavior`**
Type: "native" | "aria"
Default: "native"
Description: Whether to use native HTML form validation to prevent form submission when the value is missing or invalid, or mark the field as required or invalid via ARIA.

#### Events

**`onOpenChange`**
Type: (isOpen: boolean, menuTrigger?: MenuTriggerAction) => void
Description: Method that is called when the open state of the menu changes. Returns the new open state and the action that caused the opening of the menu.

**`onSelectionChange`**
Type: (key: Key | null) => void
Description: Handler that is called when the selection changes..

**`onInputChange`**
Type: (value: string) => void
Description: Handler that is called when the ComboBox input value changes.

### ComboboxInput

#### Props

**`endElement`**
Type: React.ReactNode
Description: Custom end element for the input.

**`endElementProps`**
Type: React.ComponentProps<typeof Button>
Description: Props for the end element button.

### ComboboxItem

#### Props

**`value`**
Type: string
Description: The value of the item.

### ComboboxList

#### Props

**`children`**
Type: React.ReactNode
Description: The children of the list.

### ComboboxPopover

#### Props

**`children`**
Type: React.ReactNode
Description: The children of the popover.

### ComboboxSection

#### Props

**`title`**
Type: string
Description: The title of the section.

### ComboboxItem

#### Props

**`value`**
Type: string
Description: The value of the item.

### ComboboxLabel

#### Props

**`children`**
Type: React.ReactNode
Description: The children of the label.

### ComboboxDescription

#### Props

**`children`**
Type: React.ReactNode
Description: The children of the description.

# Dialog

[Modal docs](https://react-spectrum.adobe.com/react-aria/Modal.html)
[Dialog docs](https://react-spectrum.adobe.com/react-aria/Dialog.html)

## Anatomy

A dialog is an overlay shown above other content in an application.

## Example

Here's a basic example of how to use the Dialog component:

```tsx
import {
  Button,
  Dialog,
  DialogContent,
  DialogDescription,
  DialogFooter,
  DialogHeader,
  DialogTitle,
  DialogTrigger,
} from "@vela-ui/react"

export function Basic() {
  return (
    <DialogTrigger>
      <Button variant="outline">Open Dialog</Button>
      <Dialog>
        <DialogContent>
          <DialogHeader>
            <DialogTitle>Edit profile</DialogTitle>
            <DialogDescription>
              Make changes to your profile here. Click save when you're done.
            </DialogDescription>
          </DialogHeader>
          <div className="grid gap-4 py-4">
            <div className="grid grid-cols-4 items-center gap-4">
              <label htmlFor="name" className="text-right">
                Name
              </label>
              <input id="name" defaultValue="Pedro Duarte" className="col-span-3" />
            </div>
            <div className="grid grid-cols-4 items-center gap-4">
              <label htmlFor="username" className="text-right">
                Username
              </label>
              <input id="username" defaultValue="@peduarte" className="col-span-3" />
            </div>
          </div>
          <DialogFooter>
            <Button type="submit">Save changes</Button>
          </DialogFooter>
        </DialogContent>
      </Dialog>
    </DialogTrigger>
  )
}
```

### Alert Dialog

Use Dialog with alertdialog role for important confirmations:

```tsx
import {
  Button,
  Dialog,
  DialogContent,
  DialogDescription,
  DialogFooter,
  DialogHeader,
  DialogTitle,
  DialogTrigger,
} from "@vela-ui/react"

export function AlertDialog() {
  return (
    <DialogTrigger>
      <Button variant="destructive">Delete Account</Button>
      <Dialog role="alertdialog">
        <DialogContent>
          <DialogHeader>
            <DialogTitle>Are you absolutely sure?</DialogTitle>
            <DialogDescription>
              This action cannot be undone. This will permanently delete your account and remove
              your data from our servers.
            </DialogDescription>
          </DialogHeader>
          <DialogFooter>
            <Button variant="outline">Cancel</Button>
            <Button variant="destructive">Delete</Button>
          </DialogFooter>
        </DialogContent>
      </Dialog>
    </DialogTrigger>
  )
}
```

## API Reference

### Dialog

#### Props

**`showCloseButton`**
Type: boolean
Default: true
Description: Whether to show the close button.

**`size`**
Type: "xs" | "sm" | "md" | "lg" | "xl" | "2xl" | "3xl" | "4xl" | "5xl" | "full"
Description: The size of the modal.

**`placement`**
Type: "top" | "center" | "bottom"
Default: "center"
Description: The placement of the modal.

**`scrollBehavior`**
Type: "inside" | "outside"
Default: "outside"
Description: How the modal handles scrolling.

**`isBlurred`**
Type: boolean
Default: false
Description: Whether to blur the background.

**`isDismissable`**
Type: boolean
Default: true
Description: Whether to close the modal when the user interacts outside it.

**`isEntering`**
Type: boolean
Description: Whether the modal is currently performing an entry animation.

**`isExiting`**
Type: boolean
Description: Whether the modal is currently performing an exit animation.

**`isKeyboardDismissDisabled`**
Type: boolean
Default: false
Description: Whether pressing the escape key to close the modal should be disabled.

**`shouldCloseOnInteractOutside`**
Type: (element: Element) => boolean
Description: When user interacts with the argument element outside of the overlay ref, return true if onClose should be called.

**`isOpen`**
Type: boolean
Description: Whether the overlay is open by default (controlled).

**`defaultOpen`**
Type: boolean
Description: Whether the overlay is open by default (uncontrolled).

#### Events

**`onOpenChange`**
Type: (isOpen: boolean) => void
Description: Handler that is called when the overlay's open state changes.

### DialogContent

#### Props

**`children`**
Type: React.ReactNode
Description: Children of the dialog. A function may be provided to access a function to close the dialog.

#### Accessibility

**`role`**
Type: "dialog" | "alertdialog"
Default: "dialog"
Description: The accessibility role for the dialog.

**`id`**
Type: string
Description: The element's unique identifier.

**`aria-label`**
Type: string
Description: Defines a string value that labels the current element.

**`aria-labelledby`**
Type: string
Description: Identifies the element (or elements) that labels the current element.

**`aria-describedby`**
Type: string
Description: Identifies the element (or elements) that describes the object.

**`aria-details`**
Type: string
Description: Identifies the element (or elements) that provide a detailed, extended description for the object.

### DialogTrigger

#### Props

**`children`**
Type: React.ReactNode
Description: The children of the dialog trigger.

**`isOpen`**
Type: boolean
Description: Whether the overlay is open by default (controlled).

**`defaultOpen`**
Type: boolean
Description: Whether the overlay is open by default (uncontrolled).

#### Events

**`onOpenChange`**
Type: (isOpen: boolean) => void
Description: Handler that is called when the overlay's open state changes.

### DialogHeader

#### Props

**`children`**
Type: React.ReactNode
Description: The children of the dialog header.

### DialogTitle

#### Props

**`children`**
Type: React.ReactNode
Description: The children of the dialog title.

### DialogDescription

#### Props

**`children`**
Type: React.ReactNode
Description: The children of the dialog description.

### DialogFooter

#### Props

**`children`**
Type: React.ReactNode
Description: The children of the dialog footer.

### DialogCloseIcon

#### Props

**`shape`**
Type: "circle" | "square"
Default: "circle"
Description: The shape of the close icon.

**`variant`**
Type: "default" | "destructive" | "ghost" | "link" | "outline" | "primary" | "secondary" | "accent"
Default: "ghost"
Description: The variant of the close icon.

**`size`**
Type: "xs" | "sm" | "md" | "lg" | "xl"
Default: "xs"
Description: The size of the close icon.

### DialogClose

# DisclosureGroup

# Disclosure

A disclosure is a collapsible section of content. It is composed of a header with a heading and trigger button, and a panel that contains the content.

[Disclosure docs](https://react-spectrum.adobe.com/react-aria/Disclosure.html)

A DisclosureGroup is a grouping of related disclosures, sometimes called an accordion. It supports both single and multiple expanded items.

[DisclosureGroup docs](https://react-spectrum.adobe.com/react-aria/DisclosureGroup.html)

## Props

**Disclosure Props**

- Extends: `React.ComponentProps<typeof AriaDisclosure>`

**DisclosureHeader Props**

- Extends: `React.ComponentProps<typeof AriaButton>`

**DisclosurePanel Props**

- Extends: `React.ComponentProps<typeof AriaDisclosurePanel>`

**DisclosureGroup Props**

- Extends: `React.ComponentProps<typeof AriaDisclosureGroup>`

## Example

Here's a basic example of how to use the Disclosure component:

```tsx
import { Disclosure, DisclosureHeader, DisclosurePanel } from "@vela-ui/react"

export function Basic() {
  return (
    <Disclosure className="w-80">
      <DisclosureHeader>Apples</DisclosureHeader>
      <DisclosurePanel>
        Crisp and refreshing fruit. Apples are known for their versatility and nutritional benefits.
        They come in a variety of flavors and are great for snacking, baking, or adding to salads.
      </DisclosurePanel>
    </Disclosure>
  )
}
```

### DisclosureGroup (Accordion)

Use DisclosureGroup to create an accordion:

```tsx
import { Disclosure, DisclosureGroup, DisclosureHeader, DisclosurePanel } from "@vela-ui/react"

export function Accordion() {
  return (
    <DisclosureGroup className="w-80">
      <Disclosure>
        <DisclosureHeader>What is React?</DisclosureHeader>
        <DisclosurePanel>
          React is a JavaScript library for building user interfaces, particularly web applications.
        </DisclosurePanel>
      </Disclosure>
      <Disclosure>
        <DisclosureHeader>What is TypeScript?</DisclosureHeader>
        <DisclosurePanel>
          TypeScript is a programming language developed by Microsoft. It is a strict syntactical
          superset of JavaScript.
        </DisclosurePanel>
      </Disclosure>
      <Disclosure>
        <DisclosureHeader>What is Tailwind CSS?</DisclosureHeader>
        <DisclosurePanel>
          Tailwind CSS is a utility-first CSS framework for rapidly building custom user interfaces.
        </DisclosurePanel>
      </Disclosure>
    </DisclosureGroup>
  )
}
```

# Drawer

## Anatomy

A drawer is a panel that slides in from the side of the screen. The usage of Drawer is similar to Dialog.

## Example

Here's a basic example of how to use the Drawer component:

```tsx
import {
  Button,
  Drawer,
  DrawerContent,
  DrawerHeader,
  DrawerTitle,
  DrawerBody,
  DrawerTrigger,
} from "@vela-ui/react"

export function Basic() {
  return (
    <DrawerTrigger>
      <Button variant="outline">Open Drawer</Button>
      <Drawer>
        <DrawerContent>
          <DrawerHeader>
            <DrawerTitle>Drawer Title</DrawerTitle>
          </DrawerHeader>
          <DrawerBody>This is the drawer content.</DrawerBody>
        </DrawerContent>
      </Drawer>
    </DrawerTrigger>
  )
}
```

## API Reference

### Drawer

#### Props

**`showCloseButton`**
Type: boolean
Default: true
Description: Whether to show the close button.

**`placement`**
Type: "top" | "bottom" | "left" | "right"
Default: "right"
Description: The placement of the drawer.

**`isBlurred`**
Type: boolean
Default: false
Description: Whether to blur the background.

**`isDismissable`**
Type: boolean
Default: true
Description: Whether to close the modal when the user interacts outside it.

**`isEntering`**
Type: boolean
Description: Whether the modal is currently performing an entry animation.

**`isExiting`**
Type: boolean
Description: Whether the modal is currently performing an exit animation.

**`isKeyboardDismissDisabled`**
Type: boolean
Default: false
Description: Whether pressing the escape key to close the modal should be disabled.

**`shouldCloseOnInteractOutside`**
Type: (element: Element) => boolean
Description: When user interacts with the argument element outside of the overlay ref, return true if onClose should be called.

**`isOpen`**
Type: boolean
Description: Whether the overlay is open by default (controlled).

**`defaultOpen`**
Type: boolean
Description: Whether the overlay is open by default (uncontrolled).

#### Events

**`onOpenChange`**
Type: (isOpen: boolean) => void
Description: Handler that is called when the overlay's open state changes.

### DrawerContent

same as DialogContent

### DrawerBody

#### Props

**`children`**
Type: React.ReactNode
Description: The children of the drawer body.

### DrawerHeader

same as DialogHeader

### DrawerTitle

same as DialogTitle

### DrawerDescription

same as DialogDescription

### DrawerCloseIcon

same as DialogCloseIcon

### DrawerClose

same as DialogClose

same as DialogTrigger

# Dropdown

A dropdown is a list of options that can be selected from a dropdown menu.

A listbox displays a list of options and allows a user to select one or more of them.

[ListBox docs](https://react-spectrum.adobe.com/react-aria/ListBox.html)

## Props

**DropdownItem Props**

- Extends: `ListBoxItemProps<T>` and `VariantProps<typeof dropdownItemVariants>`
- **`variant`**
  - Type: "default" | "destructive"
  - Default: "default"
  - Description: The visual variant of the dropdown item.

**DropdownSection Props**

- Extends: `SectionProps<T>`
- **`title`**
  - Type: string
  - Description: The title for the section.

## Example

Here's a basic example of how to use the Dropdown components:

```tsx
import { DropdownItem, DropdownLabel, DropdownDescription, DropdownSection } from "@vela-ui/react"

export function Basic() {
  return (
    <div className="w-64 rounded-md border p-1">
      <DropdownItem>
        <DropdownLabel>Profile</DropdownLabel>
        <DropdownDescription>View and edit your profile</DropdownDescription>
      </DropdownItem>
      <DropdownItem>
        <DropdownLabel>Settings</DropdownLabel>
        <DropdownDescription>Manage your preferences</DropdownDescription>
      </DropdownItem>
      <DropdownItem variant="destructive">
        <DropdownLabel>Sign out</DropdownLabel>
      </DropdownItem>
    </div>
  )
}
```

### With Sections

Dropdown items can be organized into sections:

```tsx
import { DropdownItem, DropdownLabel, DropdownSection } from "@vela-ui/react"

export function WithSections() {
  return (
    <div className="w-64 rounded-md border p-1">
      <DropdownSection title="Account">
        <DropdownItem>
          <DropdownLabel>Profile</DropdownLabel>
        </DropdownItem>
        <DropdownItem>
          <DropdownLabel>Settings</DropdownLabel>
        </DropdownItem>
      </DropdownSection>
      <DropdownSection title="Actions">
        <DropdownItem variant="destructive">
          <DropdownLabel>Sign out</DropdownLabel>
        </DropdownItem>
      </DropdownSection>
    </div>
  )
}
```

## Accessibility

These components include proper accessibility features:

- Uses semantic HTML elements for proper screen reader support
- Maintains proper color contrast ratios for text readability
- Supports keyboard navigation and focus management
- Provides clear visual hierarchy and state indication
- Works well with form elements and validation
- Supports ARIA attributes for screen readers
- Handles focus management and escape key behavior
- Provides proper role attributes for different component types

# Input

## Anatomy

An input is a text field that allows a user to enter text.

## Example

Here's a basic example of how to use the Input component:

```tsx
import { Input } from "@vela-ui/react"

export function Basic() {
  return <Input placeholder="Enter text..." />
}
```

### With Icons

An Input can include icons:

```tsx
import { Input, InputGroup } from "@vela-ui/react"
import { SearchIcon, UserIcon } from "lucide-react"

export function WithIcons() {
  return (
    <div className="space-y-4">
      <InputGroup startElement={<SearchIcon className="size-4" />}>
        <Input placeholder="Search..." />
      </InputGroup>
      <InputGroup endElement={<UserIcon className="size-4" />}>
        <Input placeholder="Username" />
      </InputGroup>
    </div>
  )
}
```

## API Reference

### Input

#### Props

**`size`**
Type: "xs" | "sm" | "md" | "lg" | "xl"
Default: "md"
Description: The size of the input.

### InputGroup

#### Props

**`size`**
Type: "xs" | "sm" | "md" | "lg" | "xl"
Description: The size of the input group.

**`startElement`**
Type: React.ReactNode
Description: Element to display at the start of the input.

**`endElement`**
Type: React.ReactNode
Description: Element to display at the end of the input.

**`startAddon`**
Type: React.ReactNode
Description: Addon to display at the start of the input.

**`endAddon`**
Type: React.ReactNode
Description: Addon to display at the end of the input.

A loader is a component that displays a loading state.

```tsx
import { Loader } from "@vela-ui/react"

export function Basic() {
```

**`size`**
Type: "xs" | "sm" | "md" | "lg" | "xl"
Default: "md"
Description: The size of the loader.

**`variant`**
Type: "default" | "ring" | "spin"
Default: "default"
Description: The variant of the loader.

# Menu

A menu displays a list of actions or options that a user can choose.

[Menu docs](https://react-spectrum.adobe.com/react-aria/Menu.html)

## Props

**Menu Props**

- Extends: `AriaMenuProps<T>`

**MenuItem Props**

- Extends: `AriaMenuItemProps<T>` and `VariantProps<typeof dropdownItemVariants>`
- **`variant`**
  - Type: "default" | "destructive"
  - Default: "default"
  - Description: The visual variant of the menu item.

**MenuSection Props**

- Extends: `AriaMenuSectionProps<T>`

## Example

Here's a basic example of how to use the Menu component:

```tsx
import { Button, Menu, MenuItem, MenuPopover, MenuTrigger } from "@vela-ui/react"

export function Basic() {
  return (
    <MenuTrigger>
      <Button variant="outline">Open Menu</Button>
      <MenuPopover>
        <Menu>
          <MenuItem>Profile</MenuItem>
          <MenuItem>Settings</MenuItem>
          <MenuItem variant="destructive">Sign out</MenuItem>
        </Menu>
      </MenuPopover>
    </MenuTrigger>
  )
}
```

### With Sections

A Menu can include sections to group related items:

```tsx
import { Button, Menu, MenuItem, MenuPopover, MenuSection, MenuTrigger } from "@vela-ui/react"

export function WithSections() {
  return (
    <MenuTrigger>
      <Button variant="outline">Open Menu</Button>
      <MenuPopover>
        <Menu>
          <MenuSection title="Account">
            <MenuItem>Profile</MenuItem>
            <MenuItem>Settings</MenuItem>
          </MenuSection>
          <MenuSection title="Actions">
            <MenuItem variant="destructive">Sign out</MenuItem>
          </MenuSection>
        </Menu>
      </MenuPopover>
    </MenuTrigger>
  )
}
```

# NumberField

A number field allows a user to enter a number, and increment or decrement the value using stepper buttons.

[NumberField docs](https://react-spectrum.adobe.com/react-aria/NumberField.html)

## Props

**NumberField Props**

- Extends: `FieldProps`, `React.ComponentProps<typeof AriaNumberField>`, and `VariantProps<typeof numberFieldVariants>`
- **`label`**
  - Type: string
  - Description: The label for the number field.
- **`description`**
  - Type: string
  - Description: A description for the number field.
- **`errorMessage`**
  - Type: string | ((validation: ValidationResult) => string)
  - Description: Error message to display when validation fails.
- **`size`**
  - Type: "xs" | "sm" | "md" | "lg" | "xl"
  - Default: "md"
  - Description: The size of the number field.

## Example

Here's a basic example of how to use the NumberField component:

```tsx
import { NumberField } from "@vela-ui/react"

export function Basic() {
  return (
    <NumberField
      label="Quantity"
      description="Enter the quantity"
      defaultValue={1}
      minValue={0}
      maxValue={100}
    />
  )
}
```

### With Validation

A NumberField can include validation:

```tsx
import { NumberField } from "@vela-ui/react"

export function WithValidation() {
  return (
    <NumberField
      label="Age"
      isRequired
      errorMessage="Please enter a valid age"
      minValue={0}
      maxValue={120}
    />
  )
}
```

# Popover

A popover is an overlay element positioned relative to a trigger.

[Popover docs](https://react-spectrum.adobe.com/react-aria/Popover.html)

## Props

**Popover Props**

- Extends: `React.ComponentProps<typeof AriaPopover>` and `VariantProps<typeof popoverVariants>`
- **`showArrow`**
  - Type: boolean
  - Default: false
  - Description: Whether the element should render an arrow.

## Example

Here's a basic example of how to use the Popover component:

```tsx
import { Button, Popover, PopoverTrigger } from "@vela-ui/react"

export function Basic() {
  return (
    <PopoverTrigger>
      <Button variant="outline">Open Popover</Button>
      <Popover>
        <div className="p-4">
          <h3 className="font-semibold">Popover Title</h3>
          <p>This is the popover content.</p>
        </div>
      </Popover>
    </PopoverTrigger>
  )
}
```

### With Arrow

A Popover can include an arrow:

```tsx
import { Button, Popover, PopoverTrigger } from "@vela-ui/react"

export function WithArrow() {
  return (
    <PopoverTrigger>
      <Button variant="outline">Open Popover</Button>
      <Popover showArrow>
        <div className="p-4">
          <h3 className="font-semibold">Popover with Arrow</h3>
          <p>This popover has an arrow pointing to the trigger.</p>
        </div>
      </Popover>
    </PopoverTrigger>
  )
}
```

# RadioGroup

[RadioGroup docs](https://react-spectrum.adobe.com/react-aria/RadioGroup.html)

## Anatomy

A radio group allows a user to select a single item from a list of mutually exclusive options.

## Example

Here's a basic example of how to use the RadioGroup component:

```tsx
import { Radio, RadioGroup } from "@vela-ui/react"

export function Basic() {
  return (
    <RadioGroup label="Favorite Color">
      <Radio value="red">Red</Radio>
      <Radio value="blue">Blue</Radio>
      <Radio value="green">Green</Radio>
    </RadioGroup>
  )
}
```

## API Reference

### RadioGroup

#### Props

**`label`**
Type: string
Description: The label for the radio group.

**`description`**
Type: string
Description: A description for the radio group.

**`errorMessage`**
Type: string | ((validation: ValidationResult) => string)
Description: Error message to display when validation fails.

**`orientation`**
Type: "vertical" | "horizontal"
Default: "vertical"
Description: The axis the Radio Button(s) should align with.

**`value`**
Type: string | null
Description: The current value (controlled).

**`defaultValue`**
Type: string | null
Description: The default value (uncontrolled).

**`isDisabled`**
Type: boolean
Description: Whether the input is disabled.

**`isReadOnly`**
Type: boolean
Description: Whether the input can be selected but not changed by the user.

**`isRequired`**
Type: boolean
Description: Whether user input is required on the input before form submission.

**`isInvalid`**
Type: boolean
Description: Whether the input value is invalid.

**`validate`**
Type: (value: string | null) => ValidationError
Description: A function that returns an error message if a given value is invalid.

**`validationBehavior`**
Type: 'native' | 'aria'
Default: "native"
Description: Whether to use native HTML form validation to prevent form submission when the value is missing or invalid, or mark the field as required or invalid via ARIA.

**`name`**
Type: string
Description: The name of the input element, used when submitting an HTML form.

**`form`**
Type: string
Description: The `<form>` element to associate the input with. The value of this attribute must be the id of a `<form>` in the same document.

#### Events

**`onChange`**
Type: (value: string) => void
Description: Handler that is called when the value changes.

**`onFocus`**
Type: (e: FocusEvent) => void
Description: Handler that is called when the element receives focus.

**`onFocusChange`**
Type: (isFocused: boolean) => void
Description: Handler that is called when the element's focus status changes.

**`onBlur`**
Type: (e: FocusEvent) => void
Description: Handler that is called when the element loses focus.

#### Accessibility

**`id`**
Type: string
Description: The element's unique identifier.

**`aria-label`**
Type: string
Description: Defines a string value that labels the current element.

**`aria-labelledby`**
Type: string
Description: Identifies the element (or elements) that labels the current element.

**`aria-describedby`**
Type: string
Description: Identifies the element (or elements) that describes the object.

**`aria-details`**
Type: boolean
Description: Identifies the element (or elements) that provide a detailed, extended description for the object.

**`aria-errormessage`**
Type: string
Description: Identifies the element that provides an error message for the object.

### Radio

#### Props

**`variant`**
Type: "default" | "outline"
Default: "default"
Description: The variant of the radio button.

**`size`**
Type: "sm" | "md" | "lg"
Default: "md"
Description: The size of the radio button.

**`value`**
Type: string
Description: The value of the radio button, used when submitting an HTML form.

**`inputRef`**
Type: React.RefObject`HTMLInputElement` | null
Description: A ref for the HTML input element.

**`isDisabled`**
Type: boolean
Description: Whether the radio button is disabled or not. Shows that a selection exists, but is not available in that circumstance.

**`autoFocus`**
Type: boolean
Description: Whether the element should receive focus on render.

#### Events

**`onFocus`**
Type: (e: FocusEvent) => void
Description: Handler that is called when the element receives focus.

**`onFocusChange`**
Type: (isFocused: boolean) => void
Description: Handler that is called when the element's focus status changes.

**`onBlur`**
Type: (e: FocusEvent) => void
Description: Handler that is called when the element loses focus.

#### Accessibility

**`id`**
Type: string
Description: The element's unique identifier.

**`aria-label`**
Type: string
Description: Defines a string value that labels the current element.

**`aria-labelledby`**
Type: string
Description: Identifies the element (or elements) that labels the current element.

**`aria-describedby`**
Type: string
Description: Identifies the element (or elements) that describes the object.

**`aria-details`**
Type: boolean
Description: Identifies the element (or elements) that provide a detailed, extended description for the object.

# Select

A select is a dropdown menu that allows a user to select a single item from a list of options.

## Props

**Select Props**

- Extends: `AriaSelectProps<T>`
- **`label`**
  - Type: string
  - Description: The label for the select.
- **`description`**
  - Type: string
  - Description: A description for the select.
- **`errorMessage`**
  - Type: string | ((validation: ValidationResult) => string)
  - Description: Error message to display when validation fails.
- **`size`**
  - Type: "xs" | "sm" | "md" | "lg"
  - Default: "md"
  - Description: The size of the select.

## Example

Here's a basic example of how to use the Select component:

```tsx
import { Select, SelectItem, SelectPopover, SelectTrigger, SelectValue } from "@vela-ui/react"

export function Basic() {
  return (
    <Select label="Favorite Fruit">
      <SelectTrigger>
        <SelectValue placeholder="Select a fruit" />
      </SelectTrigger>
      <SelectPopover>
        <SelectItem>Apple</SelectItem>
        <SelectItem>Banana</SelectItem>
        <SelectItem>Orange</SelectItem>
        <SelectItem>Grapes</SelectItem>
      </SelectPopover>
    </Select>
  )
}
```

### With Sections

A Select can include sections to group related items:

```tsx
import {
  Select,
  SelectItem,
  SelectPopover,
  SelectSection,
  SelectTrigger,
  SelectValue,
} from "@vela-ui/react"

export function WithSections() {
  return (
    <Select label="Food Category">
      <SelectTrigger>
        <SelectValue placeholder="Select a category" />
      </SelectTrigger>
      <SelectPopover>
        <SelectSection title="Fruits">
          <SelectItem>Apple</SelectItem>
          <SelectItem>Banana</SelectItem>
          <SelectItem>Orange</SelectItem>
        </SelectSection>
        <SelectSection title="Vegetables">
          <SelectItem>Cabbage</SelectItem>
          <SelectItem>Broccoli</SelectItem>
          <SelectItem>Carrots</SelectItem>
        </SelectSection>
      </SelectPopover>
    </Select>
  )
}
```

# Slider

[Slider docs](https://react-spectrum.adobe.com/react-aria/Slider.html)

## Anatomy

A slider allows a user to select one or more values within a range.

## Example

Here's a basic example of how to use the Slider component:

```tsx
import { Slider, SliderOutput, SliderThumb, SliderTrack } from "@vela-ui/react"

export function Basic() {
  return (
    <Slider defaultValue={[50]}>
      <SliderTrack>
        <SliderThumb />
      </SliderTrack>
      <SliderOutput />
    </Slider>
  )
}
```

## API Reference

### Slider

#### Props

**`size`**
Type: "sm" | "md" | "lg"
Default: "md"
Description: The size of the slider.

**`orientation`**
Type: "horizontal" | "vertical"
Default: "horizontal"
Description: The orientation of the slider.

**`isDisabled`**
Type: boolean
Default: false
Description: Whether the whole Slider is disabled.

**`minValue`**
Type: number
Default: 0
Description: The slider's minimum value.

**`maxValue`**
Type: number
Default: 100
Description: The slider's maximum value.

**`step`**
Type: number
Default: 1
Description: The slider's step value.

**`defaultValue`**
Type: T
Description: The default value (uncontrolled).

**`value`**
Type: T
Description: The current value (controlled).

**`onChange`**
Type: (value: T) => void
Description: Handler that is called when the value changes.

**`onChangeEnd`**
Type: (value: T) => void
Description: Fired when the slider stops moving, due to being let go.

### SliderOutput

A <SliderOutput> renders the current value of the slider as text.

### SliderTrack

The `SliderTrack` component is a grouping of one or more `SliderThumb` elements.

#### Props

**`onHoverStart`**
Type: (e: HoverEvent) => void
Description: Handler that is called when a hover interaction starts.

**`onHoverEnd`**
Type: (e: HoverEvent) => void
Description: Handler that is called when a hover interaction ends.

**`onHoverChange`**
Type: (isHovering: boolean) => void
Description: Handler that is called when the hover state changes.

### SliderThumb

The `SliderThumb` component renders an individual thumb within a `SliderTrack`.

#### Props

**`inputRef`**
Type: React.RefObject`HTMLInputElement` | null
Description: A ref for the HTML input element.

**`isDisabled`**
Type: boolean
Description: Whether the Thumb is disabled.

**`index`**
Type: number
Default: 0
Description: Index of the thumb within the slider.

**`autoFocus`**
Type: boolean
Description: Whether the element should receive focus on render.

**`name`**
Type: string
Description: The name of the input element, used when submitting an HTML form

**`form`**
Type: string
Description: The <form> element to associate the input with. The value of this attribute must be the id of a <form> in the same document.

# Switch

[Switch docs](https://react-spectrum.adobe.com/react-aria/Switch.html)

## Anatomy

A switch allows a user to turn a setting on or off.

## Example

Here's a basic example of how to use the Switch component:

```tsx
import { Switch } from "@vela-ui/react"

export function Basic() {
  return <Switch>Enable notifications</Switch>
}
```

## API Reference

### Switch

#### Props

**`size`**
Type: "sm" | "md" | "lg" | "xl"
Default: "md"
Description: The size of the switch.

**`inputRef`**
Type: React.RefObject`<HTMLInputElement>`
Description: A ref for the HTML input element.

**`defaultSelected`**
Type: boolean
Description: Whether the Switch should be selected (uncontrolled).

**`isSelected`**
Type: boolean
Description: Whether the Switch should be selected (controlled).

**`value`**
Type: boolean
Description: The value of the input element, used when submitting an HTML form.

**`isDisabled`**
Type: boolean
Description: Whether the input is disabled.

**`isReadOnly`**
Type: boolean
Description: Whether the input can be selected but not changed by the user.

**`autoFocus`**
Type: boolean
Description: Whether the element should receive focus on render.

**`name`**
Type: string
Description: The name of the input element, used when submitting an HTML form.

**`form`**
Type: string
Description: The `<form>` element to associate the input with. The value of this attribute must be the id of a `<form>` in the same document.

#### Events

**`onChange`**
Type: (isSelected: boolean) => void
Description: Handler that is called when the Switch's selection state changes.

**`onFocus`**
Type: (e: FocusEvent) => void
Description: Handler that is called when the element receives focus.

**`onFocusChange`**
Type: (isFocused: boolean) => void
Description: Handler that is called when the element's focus status changes.

**`onBlur`**
Type: (e: FocusEvent) => void
Description: Handler that is called when the element loses focus.

#### Accessibility

**`id`**
Type: string
Description: The element's unique identifier.

**`aria-controls`**
Type: string
Description: Identifies the element (or elements) whose contents or presence are controlled by the current element.

**`aria-label`**
Type: string
Description: Defines a string value that labels the current element.

**`aria-labelledby`**
Type: string
Description: Identifies the element (or elements) that labels the current element.

**`aria-describedby`**
Type: string
Description: Identifies the element (or elements) that describes the object.

**`aria-details`**
Type: boolean
Description: Identifies the element (or elements) that provide a detailed, extended description for the object.

# Tabs

[Tabs docs](https://react-spectrum.adobe.com/react-aria/Tabs.html)

## Anatomy

Tabs organize content into multiple sections and allow users to navigate between them.

## Example

Here's a basic example of how to use the Tabs component:

```tsx
import { Tab, TabList, TabPanel, Tabs } from "@vela-ui/react"

export function Basic() {
  return (
    <Tabs>
      <TabList>
        <Tab id="tab1">Tab 1</Tab>
        <Tab id="tab2">Tab 2</Tab>
        <Tab id="tab3">Tab 3</Tab>
      </TabList>
      <TabPanel id="tab1">Content for Tab 1</TabPanel>
      <TabPanel id="tab2">Content for Tab 2</TabPanel>
      <TabPanel id="tab3">Content for Tab 3</TabPanel>
    </Tabs>
  )
}
```

## API Reference

### Tabs

#### Props

**`variant`**
Type: "default" | "underline" | "pills"
Default: "default"
Description: The visual variant of the tabs.

**`size`**
Type: "sm" | "md" | "lg"
Default: "md"
Description: The size of the tabs.

**`orientation`**
Type: "horizontal" | "vertical"
Default: "horizontal"
Description: The orientation of the tabs.

**`isDisabled`**
Type: boolean
Default: false
Description: Whether the TabList is disabled. Shows that a selection exists, but is not available in that circumstance.

**`disabledKeys`**
Type: Iterable`<Key>`
Description: The item keys that are disabled. These items cannot be selected, focused, or otherwise interacted with.

**`selectedKey`**
Type: Key | null
Default: false
Description: The currently selected key in the collection (controlled).

**`defaultSelectedKey`**
Type: Key
Description: The initial selected key in the collection (uncontrolled).

**`keyboardActivation`**
Type: 'automatic' | 'manual'
Default: 'automatic'
Description: Whether tabs are activated automatically on focus or manually.

#### Events

**`onSelectionChange`**
Type: (key: Key) => void
Description: Handler that is called when the selection changes.

#### Accessibility

**`id`**
Type: string
Description: The element's unique identifier.

**`aria-label`**
Type: string
Description: Defines a string value that labels the current element.

**`aria-labelledby`**
Type: string
Description: Identifies the element (or elements) that labels the current element.

**`aria-describedby`**
Type: string
Description: Identifies the element (or elements) that describes the object.

**`aria-details`**
Type: boolean
Description: Identifies the element (or elements) that provide a detailed, extended description for the object.

### TabList

#### Props

**`dependencies`**
Type: ReadonlyArray
Description:Values that should invalidate the item cache when using dynamic collections.

**`items`**
Type: Iterable`<T>`
Description: Item objects in the collection.

### Tab

#### Props

**`id`**
Type: Key
Description: The unique id of the tab.

**`isDisabled`**
Type: boolean
Description: Whether the tab is disabled.

**`href`**
Type: string
Description: A URL to link to.

**`hrefLang`**
Type: string
Description: Hints at the human language of the linked URL

**`target`**
Type: "\_blank" | "\_self" | "\_parent" | "\_top"
Description: The target window for the link.

**`rel`**
Type: string
Description: The relationship between the linked resource and the current page.

**`download`**
Type: boolean | string
Description: Causes the browser to download the linked URL. A string may be provided to suggest a file name.

**`routerOptions`**
Type: RouterOptions
Description: Options for the configured client side router.

### TabPanel

#### Props

**`shouldForceMount`**
Type: boolean
Default: false
Description: Whether to mount the tab panel in the DOM even when it is not currently selected. Inactive tab panels are inert and cannot be interacted with. They must be styled appropriately so this is clear to the user visually.

**`id`**
Type: Key
Description: The unique id of the tab.

**`isDisabled`**
Type: boolean
Description: Whether the tab panel is disabled.

**`children`**
Type: React.ReactNode
Description: The children of the component. A function may be provided to alter the children based on component state.

# TextField

[TextField docs](https://react-spectrum.adobe.com/react-aria/TextField.html)

## Anatomy

A text field allows a user to enter a plain text value with a keyboard.

## Example

Here's a basic example of how to use the TextField component:

```tsx
import { TextField } from "@vela-ui/react"

export function Basic() {
  return (
    <TextField
      label="Email"
      placeholder="Enter your email"
      description="We'll never share your email"
    />
  )
}
```

## API Reference

### TextField

#### Props

**`label`**
Type: string
Description: The label for the text field.

**`description`**
Type: string
Description: A description for the text field.

**`errorMessage`**
Type: string | ((validation: ValidationResult) => string)
Description: Error message to display when validation fails.

**`size`**
Type: "xs" | "sm" | "md" | "lg" | "xl"
Description: The size of the text field.

**`startElement`**
Type: React.ReactNode
Description: Element to display at the start of the input.

**`endElement`**
Type: React.ReactNode
Description: Element to display at the end of the input.

**`isInvalid`**
Type: boolean
Description: Whether the value is invalid.

**`isDisabled`**
Type: boolean
Description: Whether the input is disabled.

**`isReadOnly`**
Type: boolean
Description: Whether the input can be selected but not changed by the user.

**`isRequired`**
Type: boolean
Description: Whether user input is required on the input before form submission.

**`validate`**
Type: (value: string) => ValidationError
Description: A function that returns an error message if a given value is invalid.

**`autoFocus`**
Type: boolean
Description: Whether the element should receive focus on render.

**`value`**
Type: string
Description: The current value (controlled).

**`defaultValue`**
Type: string
Description: The default value (uncontrolled).

**`autoComplete`**
Type: string
Description: Describes the type of autocomplete functionality the input should provide if any.

**`maxLength`**
Type: number
Description: The maximum number of characters supported by the input.

**`minLength`**
Type: number
Description: The minimum number of characters required by the input.

**`pattern`**
Type: string
Description: Regex pattern that the value of the input must match to be valid.

**`type`**
Type: 'text'| 'search'| 'url'| 'tel'| 'email'| 'password' | string
Description: The type of input to render.

**`inputMode`**
Type: 'none' | 'text' | 'tel' | 'url' | 'email' | 'numeric' | 'decimal' | 'search'
Description:Hints at the type of data that might be entered by the user while editing the element or its contents.

**`name`**
Type: string
Description: The name of the input element, used when submitting an HTML form.

**`form`**
Type: string
Description: The `<form>` element to associate the input with. The value of this attribute must be the id of a `<form>` in the same document.

**`validationBehavior`**
Type: "native" | "aria"
Default: "native"
Description: Whether to use native HTML form validation to prevent form submission when the value is missing or invalid, or mark the field as required or invalid via ARIA.

#### Events

**`onFocus`**
Type: (e: FocusEvent<T>) => void
Description: Handler that is called when the element receives focus.

**`onFocusChange`**
Type: (isFocused: boolean) => void
Description: Handler that is called when the element's focus status changes.

**`onBlur`**
Type: (e: FocusEvent<T>) => void
Description: Handler that is called when the element loses focus.

**`onChange`**
Type: (value: T) => void
Description: Handler that is called when the value changes.

```tsx
import { Textarea } from "@vela-ui/react"

export function Basic() {
```

#### Props

**`size`**

Description: The size of the textarea.

# Tooltip

[Tooltip docs](https://react-spectrum.adobe.com/react-aria/Tooltip.html)

## Anatomy

A tooltip displays a description of an element on hover or focus.

## Example

Here's a basic example of how to use the Tooltip component:

```tsx
import { Button, Tooltip, TooltipTrigger } from "@vela-ui/react"

export function Basic() {
  return (
    <TooltipTrigger>
      <Button variant="outline">Hover me</Button>
      <Tooltip>This is a tooltip</Tooltip>
    </TooltipTrigger>
  )
}
```

## API Reference

### TooltipTrigger

#### Props

**`children`**
Type: React.ReactNode
Description: The children of the tooltip trigger.

**`isDisabled`**
Type: boolean
Description: Whether the tooltip should be disabled, independent from the trigger.

**`delay`**
Type: number
Default: 1500
Description: The delay time for the tooltip to show up.

**`closeDelay`**
Type: number
Default: 500
Description: The delay time for the tooltip to close

**`trigger`**
Type: "focus"
Description: By default, opens for both focus and hover. Can be made to open only for focus.

**`isOpen`**
Type: boolean
Description: Whether the overlay is open by default (controlled).

**`defaultOpen`**
Type: boolean
Description: Whether the overlay is open by default (uncontrolled).

#### Events

**`onOpenChange`**
Type: (isOpen: boolean) => void
Description: Handler that is called when the overlay's open state changes.

### Tooltip

#### Props

**`showArrow`**
Type: boolean
Default: false
Description: Whether the element should render an arrow.

**`triggerRef`**
Type: React.RefObject`Element` | null
Description: The ref for the element which the tooltip positions itself with respect to.

**`isEntering`**
Type: boolean
Description: Whether the tooltip is currently performing an entry animation.

**`isExiting`**
Type: boolean
Description: Whether the tooltip is currently performing an exit animation.

**`placement`**
Type: "top" | "bottom" | "left" | "right"
Default: "top"
Description: The placement of the tooltip with respect to the trigger.

**`containerPadding`**
Type: number
Default: 12
Description: The placement padding that should be applied between the element and its surrounding container.

**`offset`**
Type: number
Default: 0
Description: The additional offset applied along the main axis between the element and its anchor element.

**`crossOffset`**
Type: number
Default: 0
Description: The additional offset applied along the cross axis between the element and its anchor element.

**`arrowBoundaryOffset`**
Type: number
Default: 0
Description: The minimum distance the arrow's edge should be from the edge of the overlay element.

**`shouldFlip`**
Type: boolean
Default: true
Description: Whether the element should flip its orientation (e.g. top to bottom or left to right) when there is insufficient room for it to render completely.

**`isOpen`**
Type: boolean
Description: Whether the element is rendered.

**`defaultOpen`**
Type: boolean
Description: Whether the overlay is open by default (uncontrolled).

#### Events

**`onOpenChange`**
Type: (isOpen: boolean) => void
Description: Handler that is called when the overlay's open state changes.

#### Accessibility

**`aria-label`**
Type: string
Description: Defines a string value that labels the current element.

**`aria-labelledby`**
Type: string
Description: Identifies the element (or elements) that labels the current element.

**`aria-describedby`**
Type: string
Description: Identifies the element (or elements) that describes the object.

**`aria-details`**
Type: string
Description: Identifies the element (or elements) that provide a detailed, extended description for the object.
